Sheikh Zulfiqur Bulbul Chowdhury, Advocate—For the Appellants.

parties:
Rezaul Karim and others ----- Appellants 
Vs.
Moulana Md Harun-ur-Rashid and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Siddiqur Rahman Miah J: This appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 31-8-1989 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong in, Partition Suit No. 409 of 1984 decreeing the suit.

2. The case of the plaintiff-respondent is that the land of schedule 'A' together with other land of RS khatian No. 246 of Mouza Lalkhan Bazar formerly PS Kotwali, at present PS Double Mooring, District Chittagong originally belonged to Sailendra Krishna, Pram Krishna and Gokhul Krishna, sons of late Bajendra Kumar Roy in 131/2 annas share and Harendra Kumar, son of Ajit Chandra Roy in 21 annas share; that accordingly RS khatian was prepared and finally published in the name of aforesaid owners; that by amicable arrangement; Harendra Kumar surrendered his share in the land of said khatian in favour of Sailendra Krishna, Pran Krishna and Gokhul Krishan and they were in possession of the same on payment of rent to the superior owners and that subsequently the aforesaid owners transferred their interest in the suit khatian to their wives Mrs Lalita Roy, Purnarama Roy and Rajubala Roy respectively.

3. It is stated that major portion of the said khatian was hilly jungle land and a part of it including schedule-A was ballad; that aforesaid original owners used to possess the same by giving lease to tenants; that accordingly, out of schedule 'A' land, the aforesaid original owners leased out 0.140 sahasrangsha i.e. 7 gandas of land, as described in schedule 'B' to defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, on 19-7-1938 by acceptance of salami and rent and that the defendant No. 31 Khaled Solaiman used to possess the lease-hold land by cultivating it through abraders on payment of rent to the landlords and their transferees who recognized and admitted defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman as raiyat under them. It is further stated that subsequently, with the expansion of Chittagong town, habitation and construction of dwelling houses started in the surrounding land; that accordingly, the defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, also constructed 2 kutcha dwelling houses in part of the schedule 'B' land which appertained to Municipal holding No. 150 and was possessing the same on payment of rents and taxes and thus the defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, was in possession of the schedule 'B' land as tenant and by exercising his own right openly and adversely to other defendants for over statutory period of limitation; that while the defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, was in khas possession of the entire schedule 'B' land, he sold 4 gandas equivalent to 0.80 sataks as described in schedule 'B'(1) together with the house appertaining to Municipal holding No. 150 to the plaintiff by a registered kabala dated 27th May, 1977 for valuable consideration and put the plaintiff in possession of the same.

4. The further case of the plaintiff is that after purchase, the plaintiff constructed one more kootchar house on schedule B(1) land and repaired the previous houses and let out to six temporary tenants and that the plaintiff has also undertaken construction of a 4-storied building on. part of schedule B(1) land and has completed construction of ground floor, safety tank and pucca boundary wall as per plan of CDA approved vide BC case No. 467 of 1977 and installed WASA water lines and electric lines and that on the basis of plaintiff's purchase deed and possession the name of the plaintiff has been recorded, in draft BS khatian.

5. It is further stated that Saleh Ahmed, predecessor of defendants Nos. 1 to 9 and 10 to 15, filed Title Suit No. 29 of 1959 in the court of the Subordinate Judge, First Court, Chittagong for declaration of tenancy khas dakhali right in 4 kanis of land out of which 19½ gandas in schedule 'A' and balance in RS plot Nos. 60 and 67 of khatian No. 246 on the allegation that the aforesaid owners granted 9 years' lease of 4 Kanis of land of RS plot Nos. 60, 66, 67 to one Pitambar; that Pitamber died leaving son Mukhia Jamadar and he was in possession of the same and while in possession he sold 4 kanis of land to Abdus Sobhan Chowdhury, predecessor or defendants Nos. 1 to 15 and put him in possession of the land except the land covered by a house in which the seller was in permissive possession for some time and that subsequently, Mukhia did not give possession of house and also denied their title and hence they filed the said suit.

6. It is further stated that the suit was contested by Mukhia denying the title of defendant Nos. 1 to 15 but ultimately the suit was decreed in part upto the High Court declaring title of defendant Nos. 10 to 15 and Salah Ahmed, predecessor of defendant Nos. 1 to 9 in 3 kanis 7 gandas, 3 karas of land of RS plots Nos. 60, 66 and 67; that thus by that decree of that suit, the title of defendant Nos. 1 to 15 in 19½ gandas in suit plot having been declared and they became co-sharers of plaintiff's predecessor, the defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman and the plaintiff. It is also stated that though the defendant Nos. 10 to 15 and Saleh Ahmed, predecessor of defendant Nos. 1 to 9, sought decree for declaration of title and also confirmation of possession but they did not impaled in the suit other co-sharers of suit plots; that the defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman predecessor of plaintiff was also not imp leaded in the suit and he was ignorant about the same ; that in fact, there was no partition of the land of suit RS plot No. 66 amongst 'the co-sharers by metes and bounds at any time and they were merely in convenient possession of the same and that as the other co-sharer tenants were not parties in the said suit, the said decree is not binding o n them and, on the basis of same, the defendant Nos. 1 to 15 cannot disturb the possession of the plaintiff and other defendants without partition of the same by metes and bounds.

7. It is also stated that the defendant Nos. 16 to 30 are also in possession of RS plot No. 66 by purchase from the original lessee of the landlords and their transferees and, as such, they are also co-sharers in RS plot No. 66; that the plaintiff requested the defendant Nos. 1 to 15 for partition of the land of RS plot No. 66 in suit but they did not pay any heed to it.

8. The further case of the plaintiff is that on 19-4-1978 the defendant Nos. 1 to 15 on the basis of an order passed in other Execution Case No. 3 of 1976 went to demolish the house of plaintiff, Mahabubur Rahman, predecessor of defendant Nos. 16, 21, Nasser Ali, predecessor of defendant Nos. 24 to 27 and Ayub Ali and Ayesha Akhter, defendant Nos. 22 and 23; that the plaintiff and aforesaid persons there-fore hurriedly filed Other Suit No. 50 of 1978 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong challenging the aforesaid decree passed in Other Suit No. 29 of 1959 and also prayed for temporary injunction for restraining the defendant Nos. 1 to 15 from entering into the land of the suit and from demolishing structure therefrom; that the learned Court was pleased to grant ad interim injunction but after contested hearing, the court vacated the order of ad interim injunction and after vacation of ad interim injunction; that the defendant Nos. 1 to 15 by virtue of said execution case, demolished the structures of defendant Nos. 22, 23 and Noor Ali, predecessor of defendant Nos. 24 to 27; that the plaintiff and Mahabubur Rahman filed Appeal against the said order and the learned Appellate Court allowed temporary injunction and hence the defendants could not disturb the plaintiff in the possession of his land and houses and that said defendants have again filed other Execution Case No. 6 of 1978 in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Chittagong and are trying to disturb the plaintiff in his possession of land and houses in schedule B(1).

9. As the defendant Nos. 1 to 15 did not agree to make amicable partition the land of the suit plot No. 66, the plaintiff is obliged to file the present suit.

10. The defendant Nos. 1 to 15 contested the suit by filing a written statement denying all material allegations of the plaint contending, inter alia, that 19 and 2 keras of land from the eastern portion of RS plot No. 66 with other land of RS plot No. 66 and 67 measuring 4 kanis within their specified boundaries belonged to ore Pitambar by settlement from Kundu Estate; that Pitamber cleared jungle and built a house thereon and that he himself possessed on payment of rent and taxes that after his death, it passed to his son and legal heir Mukhia Jamader; that Mukhia Jamader having in specific possession of the aforesaid 19 gandas 2 karas of RS plot No. 66 with other land measuring 4 Kanis, sold the same to the defendant's predecessor Abdus Sobhan Chowdhury by kabala dated 8-8-1947.

11. It is further stated that Mukhia Jamader while in possession of some portion of the purchased land of Abdus Sobhan Chowdhury, on permission, created certain fraudulent documents in the name of his wife, Bishuni and illegally inducted some persons in the said land; that the legal heirs of Abdus Sobhan Chowdhury, Saleh Ahmed, predecessor of defendant Nos. 1 to 9 and defendant Nos. 10 to 15, brought Title Suit No. 29 of 1959 in the court of Additional Subordinate Judge, Chittagong against Mukhia and other persons who were illegally in the land in collusion with Mukhia, for establishment of title and confirmation of possession and obtained decree on 10-9-1964 except some portion of RS plot No. 60; that these defendants are the owners of 19 gandas 2 Karas land of RS plot No. 66 from its eastern side within definite and specified boundary having no connection whatsoever with the rest of the land of RS plot No. 66; that this specific land was the land obtained by Mukhia Jamader by settlement from the land-lord; that Mukhia himself possessed this 19 gandas 2 karas specifically in his tenancy right with his other lands forming a separate tenancy under the landlord and by transfer from him, defendants predecessors Abdus Sobhan Chowdhury possessed the same and after his death, his legal heirs i.e. the defendants, possessed it separately and specifically forming a separate holding under separate jam having no connection with other portion of the RS plot No. 66; and that defendant's decretal land have been recorded In the PS Khatian in the name of their predecessor themselves. It is further stated that these defendants are in joint possession of their 19 gandas 2 karas land with the rest of the land of said RS plot and their holding is separate and they have no co-sharers for their land and no question of partition of their 19 ganders 2 karas land arises with the rest of land of RS plot No. 66 by metes and bounds; that the plaintiff nor his alleged vendor defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, has or had any right, title and legal possession in the suit land of schedule 'B' or 'B(1)' and that the plaintiff and the alleged vendors are very recent trespassers in the suit land who collusively created some documents and papers for the purpose of this suit and that the plaintiffs have no title and possession in the suit land and thus the suit is liable to be dismissed.

12. At the trial, the plaintiffs examined 2 witnesses while the contesting defendants also examined 2 witnesses and the parties have submitted documents in support of their respective case.

13. The learned Subordinate Judge by his impugned judgment dated 31-8-1989 decreed the suit.

14. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 31-8-1989, the defendants preferred this appeal before this court.

15. Mr Sheikh Zulfiqur Bulbul Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the appellants, submits that neither the plaintiffs nor his alleged vendor defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, has or had any right, title and legal possession in the suit land of schedule 'B' or 'B(1)'; that the plaintiffs and his alleged vendors are very recent trespassers in the suit land; that the plaintiffs in collusion with defendant's judgment-debtors in title Suit No. 29 of 1959 have fabricated certain fraudulent and spurious papers and, have filed the suit.

16. He further submits that plaintiff or the defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, acquired no right, title and possession in the suit land; that no tenancy right under the landlords was created by those fraudulent papers and that no rent was paid for any such tenancy. Mr Chowdhury further submits that the plaintiff's predecessors, Khaled Solaiman or the landlord failed to substantiate their title in Other Suit No. 50 of 1978 and thus the plaintiff is bound by the judgment in Other Suit No. 50 of 1978 and that the plaintiff's predecessor, Khaled Solaiman also failed to prove his lease from the landlord and he acquired no title in the suit land. He further submits that the learned Subordinate Judge, without properly applying his judicial mind to facts and circumstances of the case and materials on record, illegally passed the impugned judgment and thus the impugned judgment and decree is not tenable in law and the same is liable to be set aside.

17. Mr Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the appellants, refers to the decision in the case of Gopinath Chakrovarti and others vs Umakanta Das and others ILR 169, in the case of Ktitscbosh Mytee vs Rarndhun Kharah, WR Volvo p 526 and in the case of Surja Kanta Acharjee vs Baneswar Shaha in support of his contention.

18. Mr Omar Faruque, the learned Advocate for the respondents, submits that the land in schedule A together with other land of RS khatian No. 246 of mouza Lalkhan Bazar formerly PS Kotwali, at present PS Double Mooring, District Chittagong originally belonged to Sailendra Krishna, Pram Krishna and Gokul Krishna in 13½ annas share and Harendra Kumar in 2½ annas share; that accordingly, RS khatian was prepared and finally published in the name of aforesaid owners; that by amicable arrangement, Harendra Kumar surrendered his share in the land of said khatian in favour of Sailendra Krishna, Pram Krishna and Gokul Krishna and they were in possession of the same on payment of rent to the superior landlord and that the subsequently aforesaid owner transferred their interest in the suit khatian to their wives Mrs Lalita Roy, Purnarama Roy and Rajubala Roy respectively. He further submits their the original owners used to possess the same by giving lease to tenants; that accordingly out of schedule 'A' land, the aforesaid original owners leased out 0.140 sahasrangsha i.e. 7 gandas of land as described in schedule 'B' to defendant No. 31 Khaled Solaiman, that while the defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, was in khas possession of the entire schedule 'B' land, he sold 4 gandas equivalent to 0.80 sataks as described in schedule B(1) together with the house appertaining to Municipal holding No. 150 to the plaintiff by a registered kabala dated 27th May, 1977 for valuable consideration and put the plaintiff in possession of the same. It is further submitted that after purchase the plaintiff constructed one more kutcha house on schedule B(1) land and repaired the previous houses and let out to 6 temporary tenants. The plaintiff Moulana Mohammad Harun-ur-Rashid has also undertaken construction of 4-storied building on part of schedule B(1) land and has completed construction of ground floor, safety tank and pucca boundary wall as per plan of CDA approved plan vide BC Case No. 467 of 1977 and installed WASA water lines and electric lines. It is further submitted that the defendants title in 19½ gandas in suit plot has been declared but in the aforesaid plot the total area of land is 41½ kanis which is much in excess of the land of the share of defendant Nos. 1 to 15; that the original, landlords before leasing out the land of Patambar, out of the suit plot No. 66 leased out 7½ gandas land to plaintiff's predecessor the defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, as such there is no clash of title between the plaintiff and defendants No. 1 to 15 and other co-sharers and the same is required to be partitioned. Mr Faruque further submits that the impugned judgment and decree was legally passed which should not be interfered.

19. The point for determination in this appeal is whether the learned Subordinate Judge was justified in passing the decree in the suit.

20. In order to arrive at a correct decision on the contention of the learned Advocates of the contesting parties, it is necessary to scrutinise the evidence on record.

21. It is established principle of law that the burden of proof lies on the party who substantially asserts the affirmative of the issue and not upon the party who denies it. Moreover, it is but reasonable and just that the suitor who relies upon the existence of a fact, should be called upon to prove his own case. The party on who; the onus of proof lies must, in order to succeed, establish a prima facie case. He cannot, on failure to do so, take advantage of the weakness of his adversary's case. He must succeed by the strength of his own right and the clearness of his own proof.

22. Here the case of the plaintiff, Moulana Md. Harun-ur-Rashid, is that the original owners namely Sailendra Krishna, Pram Krishna and Gokul Krishna who transferred the land to their wives namely, Mrs Lalita Roy, Purnarama Roy and Rajubala Roy who leased out 0.140 sahasrangsha i.e. 7 gandas, of land as described in schedule B to defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, on 19-7-1938 by acceptance of salami and rent and subsequently Khaled Solaiman sold 4 ganjas equivalent to 0.80 stakes with structures described in B(1) to the plaintiff by registered kabala dated 27th May, 1977 for valuable consideration and thus the plaintiff created structure and has been living therein.

23. This assertion of the plaintiff has no Value unless such assertion is proved by credible evidence.

24. Firstly, we have to see whether the lease from Lolita Roy, Purnarama Roy and Rajubala Roy to Khaled Solaiman has been proved.

25. The contention of the contesting defendants is that the paper of lease is forged which were collusively created. It is admitted that there is no registered document in respect of such lease. The plaintiffs have filed 7 rent receipts.

<u>26. Since the contesting defendants have denied the genuineness of these rent receipts, the plaintiff is to prove the genuineness of these rent receipts. The rule of law is that the landlord or his authorized agent has to come to the court to prove such rent receipts. Now let us see how far these rent receipts have been proved.</u>

27. The plaintiff, in support of his case, has submitted 7 rent receipts which are mar-ked exhibit 2(ka), 2(kha), 2(ga), 2(gha), 2(oma), 2(cha) and 2(jha) which were granted by the same person on behalf of the original landlords. The plaintiff has examined 2 witnesses in support of his contention.

28. PW 1 Harun-ur-Rashid and PW-2 Madhu Sudan Das.

<u>29. PW 1 Harun-ur-Rashid deposed that the defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, took lease 7 ganders of land from the original land-lord. In cross examination, he admitted that there is no patta or registered deed in support of such settlement; that he was not present at the time of settlement nor has he any knowledge about that settlement.</u>

<u>30. PW 2, Madhu Sudan Das, admitted in his deposition that at the time of writing dakhilas he was not present and dakhilas were written by Salam and Avinish. He further deposed that Salam and Avinish were the Tahashilders under original landlord. There is no document to prove that Salam and Avinish were the Tahashilders under the original landlord and these rent receipts have neither been proved by the landlord nor have these rent receipts been proved by his authorised agent. PW 2 has not deposed that he was present at the time of writing of these rent receipts nor did he depose that he knows the signatures of Salam and Avinish. Moreover, the solitary evidence of PW 2 without any corroborative evidence cannot be relied upon. Thus the factum of alleged lease has not been proved in any way. Moreso, the appearance of these rent receipts seem to be fraudulent and spurious when the lease of Khaled Solaiman has not been proved, then the subsequent transfer from Khaled Solaiman to the plaintiff will have no leg to stand.</u>

<u>31. In view of the evidence, both oral and documentary, it appears to us that the plaintiff's alleged vendor defendant No. 31, Khaled Solaiman, has or had no right title and interest in the suit land. So title and interest in respect of the suit land does not pass to the plaintiffs by virtue of transfer deed dated 27-5-1977.</u>

<u>32. The undisputed fact is that the suit property is the non-agricultural property within Chittagong Municipality and the learned trial Court erred in law in not arriving at finding and decision to the effect that in the absence of registered bilateral document/ instrument, the plaintiff or his alleged vendor did not acquire any title.</u>

<u>33. There, is another aspect of this appeal. The defendant-appellants claim right title and interest in 19½ gandas in suit RS plot No. 66 along with 3 kanis 1/2 gandas = 60½ gandas in non suited plot No. 60 and 67 measuring total area of 4 kanis land by registered kabala dated 8-8-1947 from the original owner and at one point of dispute the predecessor of the defendant-appellants constrained to bring title Suit No. 29 of 1959 [subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 17 of 1961 and Title Suit No. 12 of 1962] and after contested hearing appellants predecessor obtained decree on 10-9-1964 and during trial, the suit land was investigated by Mr Saleh Ahamed Chowdhury, the learned pleader Commissioner, whose investigation report, sketch map, field book etc. have been made part of the decree of the aforesaid suit. That 19½ gandas in eastern portion of suit schedule RS plot No. 66 was given to the appellants in the aforesaid Title Suit No. 29 of 1959 subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 17 of 1961 and Title Suit No. 12 of 1962 shown in the trace map of the investigation report. Since the predecessors of the plaintiff-respondent were parties in that suit, so the plaintiff-respondent is bound by the decree of that suit. Thus the suit is barred by res judicata. The condition of res judicata is that former suit must have been a suit between the same parties or between the parties under whom they or any of them claim. This condition recognises the general principle of law that the judgment and decrees bind the parties and privies. Therefore, when it is admitted that the predecessors of the plaintiffs-respondents were the parties in Suit No. 29 of 1959 (previous No. 17 of 1961 and 12 of 1962), the judgment and decree of that suit bind the plaintiff-respondent and the present suit is barred by resjudicata. By dint of judgment and decree of aforesaid Title Suit No. 17 of 1961, the defendant-appellants put into Khas possession in maximum decretal land by the Court through execution case, but the present respondent No. 1 resisted the execution in 4 gandas by filing Title Suit No. 50 of 1978 as plaintiff in the First Court of learned Subordinate Judge, Sadar, Chittagong and his ex parte order of ad interim injunction was vacated after contested hearing by order No. 24 dated 31-7-1978 (Exhibit-Kha(1)) and the present respondent No. 1 voluntarily got the suit dismissed for default in his previous Title Suit No. 50 of 1978 by order dated 17-3-1986, but in the meantime, the respondent No.1 as plaintiff surreptitiously filed present Partition Suit No. 50 of 1979 renumbered as Partition Suit No. 409 of 1984 on 13-4-1979. The plaintiff- respondent No. 1 as his devised policy deviated from his earlier admission made in the plaint of Other Suit No. 50 of 1978 in the present suit and manufactured various forged, concocted, frivolous and fictitious documents in his favour. The learned court below arrived at erroneous finding and decision and thereby decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 31-8-1939.</u>

34. The learned Subordinate Judge without considering all material aspects of the case and material evidence on record erroneously passed the impugned judgment and decree without assigning any cogent and good reasons and his judgment is vitiated by misreading and non-reading of material evidence and misconstruction of documents. Thus the learned Subordinate Judge failed to arrive at a correct decision.

35. In the light of the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record, we are of the view that the plaintiff-respondent has totally failed to prove their case and the learned Subordinate Judge is not justified in passing the impugned judgment and decree dated 31-8-1989 which is liable to be set aside.

36. In the result, the appeal is allowed without any order as to costs and the judgment and decree dated 31-8-1989 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Chittagong in Partition Suit No. 409 of 1984 is set aside.

Send down the LCR at once.

End.
